title: Console: Fleet scaling controls, live throughput view, and audit timeline
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background:
Customers running Redwood Dedicated have requested a single control surface in Console to: 1) make deterministic scaling decisions for fleets (min/max, target throughput), 2) observe real-time and historical throughput/latency against guarantees, and 3) inspect a compact, tamper-evident change history for fleet configuration and autoscaler actions.

Goals:
- Expose granular scaling controls for fleets (scale floor/ceiling, target RPS/throughput, preferred instance types) with sensible defaults.
- Surface a live throughput dashboard that correlates request patterns, token throughput, and SLO attainment over selectable windows (1m/5m/1h/24h).
- Provide an immutable change timeline (who/what/why) for manual edits, policy updates, and autoscaler-triggered resizes with links to associated PRs/config diffs.
- Make controls safe: preview estimated cost and capacity impact, require confirmation for risky changes, and integrate automatic rollback triggers.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Users can set fleet-level min/max GPUs and a target throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec) and save a named profile.
- Live dashboard displays 1m/5m average throughput, 95th latency, queue length, and SLO breach rate; data refresh <= 10s for 1m window.
- Timeline shows entries for: manual changes, autoscaler decisions, routed-fallback events, and deployment rollouts. Each entry includes actor, timestamp, diff link, and optional reason.
- Changing scaling policy shows an estimated 72-hr cost delta and a preview of expected throughput curve; major changes require a secondary confirmation.
- Telemetry: new console metrics emitted (console.fleet.change, console.preview.cost_estimate, console.dashboard.load) and Grafana dashboard with alert when previewed autoscaler causes >30% cost increase.

Success metrics (30/60/90 days):
- 60% reduction in console-related support tickets where customers ask how to change fleet scaling policies.
- 40% fewer unexpected SLO breaches attributable to misconfigured fleet scaling.
- Adoption: 30% of active Dedicated customers create/modify fleet profiles through the console UI within 90 days.

Implementation notes:
- UX will use a two-pane workflow: left = scaling controls + cost/impact preview; right = live throughput and SLO widget.
- Backend: reuse existing autoscaler engine (ENG-4802) but add an API surface for policy preview and dry-run simulations.
- Data: throughput and latency rolled up to a 10s timeseries in metrics store for responsive rendering.
- Security: timeline entries are immutable; admin-only action to redact if required (audit log retained).

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha behind feature flag for internal + two pilot customers (2 weeks).
2) Gradual rollout to 20% of orgs with Dedicated for 2 weeks (monitor SLOs & support tickets).
3) Full rollout with documentation and in-console guided tour.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Realtime cadence vs. cost: 10s granularity chosen to balance dashboard usefulness vs metrics ingestion cost.
- Preview fidelity: simulation uses sampled historical traces and heuristics; may differ from live in bursty traffic patterns. We will add confidence bands to communicate uncertainty.

notes: Open question: should target throughput accept both tokens/sec and requests/sec? (engineering prefers tokens/sec for cost mapping).
Mitigation: expose both but prefer tokens/sec in the API and show conversion in the UI with explanation.
